task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-11-01, in the area of player absence and offensive reorganization):
How much the offense reorganizes (relative to L) predicts the change in points per possession.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): n=986; n=148, mde rho; 148 spells

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

research_concepts: offensive reorganization relative to baseline L
methodological_questions: How is baseline L defined, and how is offensive reorganization measured relative to it?
Does reorganization relative to L predict the change in points per possession after player absence?
Is the reorganization measure reliable and free of outcome-derived labels or lookahead leakage?
What sample size and minimum detectable effect does a spell-level analysis with 148 spells provide?
Which confounders (lineup quality, opponent, playoff context, season drift) must be controlled?
evidence_establishes: The retrieval call returned zero records (n_results = 0). No earlier study-family record from this project is available for this question, so no prior finding can be cited.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether reorganization relative to L predicts change in points per possession.
Whether any measure of reorganization is reliable, or what effect size is plausible.
Whether the 148-spell sample has adequate power; the stated minimum detectable effect (rho) is not given as a number.
Whether earlier work tried and failed a similar approach.
own_inferences: The task does not define L, the reorganization metric, the change window, or what counts as a spell, so the estimand cannot be fixed from the text alone.
The unit counts are ambiguous: n=986 and 148 spells are both listed, and it is unclear whether 986 are possessions, games, or player-team units.
If reorganization is built from play-type possession records that already carry points, the predictor will be mechanically linked to the outcome (OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL).
With 148 spells and a 'mde rho' listed but not valued, a modest correlation is unlikely to be detected unless the effect is large.
Using 2025-26 data as of 2026-11-01 is admissible: the regular season is complete from 2026-04-13 and the playoffs from 2026-06-21, both before the cutoff.
uncertainties: Definition of L and of offensive reorganization is missing.
Whether the 148 spells are the full analytic sample or a subset is unclear.
The numeric minimum detectable effect is missing.
Whether pre- and post-absence windows and the play-type graph are computed without using post-window points is unknown.
No historical records were available to check prior failures or known measurement problems.

historical_effect.explanation: The retrieval returned no records, so it neither supported nor blocked the question. The decision rests on the task statement and data description: the key construct L is undefined and the sample is small and ambiguously counted.

blocking_constraints.text: Reorganization relative to L has no stated operational definition or reliability check.
148 spells with an unvalued minimum detectable effect may not detect a realistic effect size.
If reorganization uses play-type points, the predictor shares the outcome's data and the association would be partly mechanical.

prior_work.summary: No prior work was returned by the tool, so whether this question has been answered earlier by this project cannot be determined.

risks.text: Reorganization and L are undefined; their reliability across games and seasons is untested.
148 spells is small for a spell-level regression, and the minimum detectable effect is not specified numerically.
Play-type records built from points may encode the outcome in the predictor.
Reorganization computed over a window that overlaps the post-absence points window would leak outcome information.
Lineup quality, minutes, opponent strength, and playoff context may drive both reorganization and points per possession.
Pooling 2022-23 through 2025-26 may mix rule, pace, and roster changes.
Multiple choices of L, window length, and outcome definition could produce a spurious significant result if all are tried.
Absence spells may be mislabeled if injury status or rotation intervals are incomplete.

design.estimand: Not yet defined. Minimum viable: the association between a pre-specified reorganization-relative-to-L index for each absence spell and the change in points per possession from a pre-absence to a post-absence window, with a stated effect size of interest.
design.unit: Player-absence spell (team-level offensive possession windows nested within spells), after the unit count is confirmed.
design.sample: Spells from the 2022-23 to 2025-26 regular seasons and playoffs available as of 2026-11-01, using only games completed before the cutoff. The 148-spell count must be verified against the 986-unit figure.
design.power: Compute power before analysis: state the minimum detectable effect as a number and derive the power for 148 spells at alpha 0.05. Proceed only if power is adequate for the pre-specified effect of interest.
design.controls: Fixed effects for season and playoff status; controls for lineup quality (net rating of remaining lineup), minutes, opponent defensive rating, and pre-absence pace. The predictor must be computed from pre-window or non-outcome features only.
design.falsification: Placebo spells with no absence (matched on lineup and minutes) and placebo windows shifted in time; the estimated association should be null in both. Also test whether reorganization predicts points in games without absence.
design.multiplicity: Pre-specify one primary definition of L and one window. Report all other definitions as sensitivity analyses with correction for the number of specifications.
design.decision_rule: Primary test: 95% CI for the standardized coefficient on reorganization relative to L. Support only if the CI excludes zero and the lower bound exceeds the pre-specified effect of interest. Reject only if the CI is within the minimum detectable effect of zero. Otherwise report as uncertain.
design.data_version: Data as of 2026-11-01: NBA 2022-23 to 2024-25 regular seasons and playoffs; 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13); 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21). Freeze the data version and log any later revisions.
